independent.summary: The signup gate is read before the work and recorded only after it (`blocked` at :148, `record` at :166, with a `User.findOne`, a bcrypt cost-12 hash and two writes in between), so the per-address ceiling only binds sequential callers: a script that opens N connections at once has every request pass `blocked` while the counter is still 0 and ends up creating ~N accounts per window instead of `perSignupIp`, which is exactly the 'as fast as it can post' case the item set out to bound. Reserving the slot before the hash (increment-then-check, rolling back on a refusal) would hold the bound under concurrency.
